acceptance_criteria.criterion: ChunkWriter(slug_dir, wp_id, stage) creates {slug_dir}/orchestrator/chunks/ if absent and opens a .jsonl file with the correct revision number.
The first line of every created JSONL file is a valid JSON object containing chunk_format, stream_mode, and langgraph_stream_version fields.
write_chunk() appends one JSON line per call and calls flush() immediately.
close() is idempotent — calling it multiple times does not raise.
The class works as a context manager (with ChunkWriter(...) as cw:).
All unit tests pass on both Unix and Windows path conventions (using pathlib.Path).
A file I/O error during write_chunk() is logged at DEBUG level and does not propagate.

comments.note: chunk_writer.py and dialogue_writer.py share identical revision-numbering logic (_next_revision / the glob-and-rsplit pattern). If a third writer is added, it would be worth extracting a shared _next_revision(dir, pattern) helper into utils/__init__.py or a small private module to eliminate the duplication. Out of scope for this WP.

dialogue_writer.py uses a bare module-level function (write_dialogue) whereas chunk_writer.py uses a class. Both are valid, but the inconsistency is mildly surprising. The class model is more appropriate here given the stateful open-file lifecycle, so no change needed.

The _CHUNK_HEADER constant is module-level and mutable (dict). A future caller could inadvertently mutate it. Freezing it with types.MappingProxyType or making it a tuple-of-pairs would be a small defensive improvement.

comments.note: write_chunk() only catches OSError (per spec). A non-JSON-serializable value (e.g. a set or custom object) causes an unhandled TypeError that propagates to the caller. This is consistent with the WP which limits suppression to file I/O errors, but callers should be made aware. Consider adding a TypeError catch with a DEBUG log in a follow-on WP if upstream callers pass untrusted chunk data.

Unicode and emoji content (including CJK characters) serializes and deserializes correctly via json.dumps with ensure_ascii=False. No encoding issues.

summary: Reviewed orchestrator/src/utils/chunk_writer.py (187 lines) and orchestrator/tests/test_chunk_writer.py (400 lines) in full. Cross-referenced dialogue_writer.py for pattern consistency.
All four review dimensions PASS: Maintainability, Best Practices, Performance, Future Context.

No Blocking issues found. No Fix-Forward changes applied (attempted MappingProxyType for _CHUNK_HEADER but reverted — json.dumps on Python 3.14 does not natively serialize MappingProxyType, confirming the change would be behavioral, not eligible for Fix-Forward).
Two Documentation-Forward items tagged for the Documentation agent.
One cross-cutting architectural note recorded at project level: shared revision-numbering logic between chunk_writer and dialogue_writer is a refactor candidate if a third writer is ever added.

comments.note: Maintainability — PASS. Module and class docstrings are exemplary: they document the public API, parameters, raises contract, JSONL file layout (with line-numbered examples), and a cross-coupling note about the parallel orchestrator/chunks vs orchestrator/dialogues directory structure. Variable names throughout are precise and self-documenting.

Best Practices — PASS. Path(slug_dir) coercion in __init__ correctly handles str inputs. __exit__ does NOT return True — exceptions propagate correctly (common pitfall avoided). _closed flag check precedes _fh is None check in both write_chunk and close, which is the correct defensive ordering. finally: self._fh = None in close() is the right pattern to prevent double-close issues. Static method _next_revision is correctly isolated.

Performance — PASS. flush() after every write is intentional per spec (durability contract). _next_revision glob+sort is O(n) over existing revision files, called once at construction. No concerns at expected scale.

Fix-Forward ATTEMPTED and REVERTED: _CHUNK_HEADER is a module-level mutable dict. Attempted to wrap with types.MappingProxyType to prevent accidental external mutation (the Developer noted this as a low-priority improvement). Reverted because Python 3.14's json.dumps does not natively serialize MappingProxyType — applying the fix would require a custom JSONEncoder, which changes the serialization code path (behavioral). This is not eligible for Fix-Forward. Reclassified as documentation-forward.

[documentation-forward] _CHUNK_HEADER is a module-level mutable dict exported from the module (imported directly in tests via 'from src.utils.chunk_writer import _CHUNK_HEADER'). The module docstring and class docstring should note that _CHUNK_HEADER is a private implementation detail and must not be mutated by callers — external mutation would silently corrupt all subsequent header writes. Consider adding a # DO NOT MUTATE comment inline on the constant as well.

[documentation-forward] write_chunk() type annotation is 'chunk: dict[str, Any]'. The docstring should clarify that non-JSON-serializable values (e.g. a set, a custom object) will raise a TypeError that propagates to the caller — only OSError from file I/O is suppressed. This distinction is critical for callers passing untrusted chunk data from upstream LangGraph streams.
